messages.content: Good news: Mark got Friday PTO approved, so Santa Fe can be Thursday through Sunday. I need to stop dithering now. Can we make the call on SAF versus Albuquerque and the hotel before those rooms disappear?

Yes. With the Thursday-Sunday dates locked, I would rank the airport plans this way: 1) Fly DEN-SAF on the Thursday afternoon nonstop and return Sunday late morning from SAF. It costs more, but it keeps the first night intact and avoids a rental-car drive after dark. 2) Fly DEN-ABQ only if the savings stay large after rental, fuel, and the extra drive time. 3) Any connection-based plan is not worth it for a short anniversary weekend unless the nonstop sells out.
The Santa Fe nonstop is running about $180 more per person than the Albuquerque option once I include the rental. That still feels annoying.

It is annoying, but for this trip I would still pay it if the budget can absorb it. Albuquerque saves money on paper, but you trade away the easy Thursday arrival, add a 60-plus minute evening drive, and make the first night more logistics-heavy. For a three-night weekend, the simpler airport is the better value unless that extra $360 is a hard stop.
Okay. If we use SAF, do we still need a car?

Yes, especially if you choose the resort outside the center. A compact rental from SAF should be enough: short airport pickup, easy hotel parking, and flexibility for dinner, Canyon Road, or a scenic drive. If you chose the downtown boutique inn instead, you could consider skipping the car and using rideshare, but the resort plan works better with a rental.
Hotel is the part I keep circling. Boutique balcony king downtown versus the resort with the pool and hot tub.

For the weekend you described, I would put the resort first. It gives you the pool, hot tub, fitness access, and easier parking, so the stay feels more like a reset. The boutique inn is the charm-and-walkability pick, and the balcony king is the strongest room feature, but no pool or hot tub is a real gap. The plaza-area hotel stays third because the convenience gets eaten up by valet cost.
Then resort. Ask for the patio or balcony, but I do not want to make that the thing that blocks the booking.

Good. Book the refundable resort room for Thursday through Sunday, request a king room with patio or balcony, and add quiet location as the fallback if that room type cannot be guaranteed. Also confirm self-parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness hours while booking so there are no surprises.
Should I hold Albuquerque as a backup too?

I would not hold a second full plan. Keep Albuquerque as a fare-check backup only until you ticket SAF. Once the Santa Fe flights are purchased, let the Albuquerque comparison go so you are not managing duplicate rentals and hotel assumptions.
All right. Give me the booking order, including seats.

Booking order: 1) Ticket the Thursday afternoon DEN-SAF nonstop and the Sunday late-morning SAF-DEN return, using a 24-hour cancellation window if available. 2) Choose window seats together or as close as the map allows; if one leg is blocked, set a reminder to check again at online check-in. 3) Book the refundable resort Thursday-Sunday with the king patio or balcony request, quiet-room fallback, and confirmed pool, hot tub, fitness, and parking. 4) Reserve a compact rental at SAF with pickup matched to the flight arrival and return about 90 minutes before the Sunday departure. 5) After confirmations land, book the anniversary dinner for Friday or Saturday once you decide which night you want to anchor around sunset.

messages.content: We leave for Santa Fe in five days. Flights, resort, and compact car are booked. Can you help me make this practical without turning it into a minute-by-minute itinerary?

Keep the structure simple: airport, arrival, one anchored dinner, and weather layers. For DEN, aim to be at the terminal about two hours before departure if you are checking a bag; closer to 90 minutes only if you are carrying on and security looks normal.
We are checking one bag and parking at DEN, so I will pad it.

Then leave home roughly 2.5 to 3 hours before departure depending on traffic, prebook parking if you can, and keep the rental confirmation handy. SAF is small, so once you land the rental pickup should be quick, then it is an easy drive to the resort.
The resort confirmed parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness. Patio request is noted but not guaranteed. What should I do with dinner timing?

For late September, plan on warm late afternoon and a cooler evening. If you want a sunset drink or view first, book dinner around 7:15. If the restaurant patio itself is the sunset moment, book closer to 6:30 or 6:45.
One wrinkle: the Sunday return seat map changed. My window seat disappeared and now we are in two aisle seats.

Do not pay a big upgrade for that short return yet. Check the map daily, then again right at the 24-hour check-in mark. If a window pair or window-plus-aisle opens in rows near you, grab it; otherwise two aisles are acceptable for the short hop home.
Can you give me the loose weekend version?

Loose version: Thursday, fly, pick up the compact car, check in, hot tub or quiet dinner. Friday, Plaza and Canyon Road, then the anniversary dinner timed around sunset. Saturday, slow breakfast, one museum or short scenic drive, pool/hot tub time, no overpacking the day. Sunday, fuel the car, return it with a buffer, and keep checking the seat map. Pack light layers: short sleeves, sweater, dinner layer, warmer jacket, comfortable walking shoes, sunglasses, and sunscreen.

messages.content: Santa Fe is off my calendar, so now I need to deal with Nashville. I was assigned to an instructor certification lab near Vanderbilt in mid-October. Sessions are Tuesday through Thursday, but there may be a Monday afternoon calibration and maybe a Thursday trainer dinner. Can you help me build the flight and hotel plan before I book anything?

Yes. First I need the exact session dates, how likely the Monday calibration is, and whether the Thursday dinner would be expected or just optional. Those two schedule details drive both the arrival day and the return flight.

Formal sessions are October 15 through 17. Monday calibration is not confirmed, but if it happens it would probably be 2 to 5. The dinner Thursday could run 6 to 8:30. The hotel block deadline is Friday.

Then I would not build this around a Monday morning arrival. Ranked arrival plan: 1) Sunday afternoon DEN-BNA nonstop, which gives you a calm start and protects the possible Monday calibration. 2) Monday morning arrival only if the coordinator confirms no calibration or says it starts late enough that a delay would not hurt. 3) Saturday arrival feels unnecessary unless you are adding personal time.
Sunday is an extra hotel night, but I do not want to be the person walking into calibration frazzled. What would Sunday arrival look like?

Fly Denver to Nashville in the afternoon, land early evening, rideshare to Midtown or Vanderbilt, check in, and keep Sunday night low-key. Monday becomes a buffer day: remote work in the morning, calibration if it happens, and time to find the lab without rushing.

The hotel choices I found are the official block right by the lab at $289, limited amenities; a Midtown suite hotel at $219 with 4.4 reviews, pool, and fitness but no listed hot tub; and a quieter West End hotel at $235 with nicer rooms, 4.5 reviews, no pool listed, and a longer rideshare.

I would rank them: 1) Midtown suite hotel, because it balances reviews, rate, pool, fitness, and workable distance. 2) Official block, best for pure convenience but expensive and thin on amenities. 3) West End, good comfort but less practical if you are going back and forth to the lab.
I really do not want a mediocre hotel on a certification week. I would use the gym; hot tub would be nice, but I can live without it.

Then Midtown is the best first hold. It clears the review concern, gives you fitness access and a pool, and the missing hot tub is the one amenity gap to note. Before committing, confirm fitness hours, pool hours, cancellation deadline, and the rideshare or walking time to the Vanderbilt lab.
Could I skip a rental car entirely?

Probably yes. If the week stays centered around Vanderbilt, rideshare is cleaner than paying for a car plus hotel parking. Rent only if the agenda adds an offsite clinic, bulky equipment transport, or a dinner far outside the central Nashville area.
I may have one rolling demo case and a laptop bag, nothing huge.

That still points to rideshare. Use a standard airport rideshare unless the case is oversized; upgrade to XL only if needed. Ask whether the lab has secure storage so you are not dragging the demo case back to the hotel or to dinner.
Flight-wise I saw Southwest cheaper, but United also had a nonstop. How should I compare that?

Compare total cost and schedule, not just the fare headline. If both are nonstop Sunday afternoon, look at baggage, change rules, arrival time, and seat selection. With a checked demo case, Southwest's included bag may erase some of the price difference. I would avoid a connecting itinerary unless it saves a lot and the layover is short and comfortable.
For the return, I do not love gambling on a Thursday night departure if that dinner happens.

Then use Friday as the planning case. Look for a late-morning or midday BNA-DEN nonstop so you can have breakfast, rideshare to the airport, and not rush after a late Thursday. If the dinner is canceled and the lab ends early, you can still compare a Thursday evening nonstop before ticketing.
Should I book the hotel before flights because of the block deadline?

Place a refundable hold at the Midtown suite hotel now and calendar the cancellation deadline. If the official block can be held with no penalty, hold one backup room before Friday, then release it once the Monday and Thursday schedule is confirmed. Flights can wait 24 to 48 hours unless fares jump; if you book before the schedule answers, use a fare with a cancellation or change window.
Give me the exact questions to send the coordinator.

Send these: 1) Is Monday calibration required, and what are the exact time and location? 2) What is the earliest safe Thursday departure if attending all required activities? 3) Is the Thursday trainer dinner mandatory, and where does it end? 4) Are there any offsite labs, clinic visits, or equipment transport needs? 5) Is secure storage available for demo cases? 6) Are there recommended hotels beyond the official block, or any shuttle arrangement? 7) Are rideshares or parking reimbursable? Working plan for now: Sunday afternoon nonstop to Nashville, refundable Midtown suite hold, no rental car unless offsite work appears, and Friday late-morning or midday nonstop back to Denver.
